blockers.title: NT-7 is half this gate's named corpus and nothing in the artifact retains evidence for it; its property survives only as an unbacked clause inside EV-2's pass property
blockers.finding: The live harness cell names two classes: 'host-must-not-mint corpus (DR-131 NT-7, NT-8)'. Read against preview-analyze-contract.v2, they are different obligations. NT-7 is host-must-not-mint-verdict, whose input is 'A host path that derives fail or warn other than from the core policyOutcome in CoreCompletion' and whose pass is 'Refused. The only policy result is core-evaluated policyOutcome. Host does not mint fail/warn.' NT-8 is host-must-not-mint-d9-or-termination-from-policy, whose input is 'A host path that mints a D9 class, exit number, or HostTermination from the pack threshold or from policyOutcome' and whose pass is 'Refused. Host maps only existing D9 v1.14 classes. policyOutcome is not HostTermination.' Now map the artifact onto them. EV-1 retains D9 class tokens and their membership in the v1.14 set — NT-8. EV-2 retains results showing core policyOutcome is not treated as HostTermination and does not become an exit or HostTermination value — NT-8. EV-3 retains a record that no D9 class, exit or HostTermination was minted from the pack threshold or policyOutcome — NT-8. All three retained-evidence members and all three exact-byte intents sit inside NT-8. Nothing anywhere retains a host path that derives fail or warn other than from the core policyOutcome. I checked mechanically: the string 'fail/warn' occurs twice in the whole artifact, both times in prose and neither time in any exactByteIntent, and 'CoreCompletion' — the anchor NT-7's input names — occurs zero times. NT-7's property does appear once, as the second sentence of EV-2's passProperty: 'Host-minted fail/warn other than core policyOutcome fails.' That sentence scores a property for which the same member's exactByteIntent retains no bytes at all. It is the exact inverse of the defect I raised against the G25 sibling, where bytes were retained that nothing scored; here a property is scored with nothing retained, and the effect is worse, because a reader scanning pass properties sees the obligation covered.
blockers.failureScenario: A fixture author builds to this specification. EV-1, EV-2 and EV-3 tell them to pin terminal results whose D9 tokens are in-set, whose policyOutcome is not treated as HostTermination, and which mint nothing from the pack threshold. Three fixtures, all exercising NT-8. None constructs a host path that derives fail or warn some other way, because no exact-byte intent asks for one. The harness runs green and NT-7 was never exercised. Nothing in the evidence cell alone reveals the gap — all three members really are NT-8 members — so only the corpus naming exposes it, and the artifact never opens the corpus.
blockers.whyItMatters: The gate's claim is two limbs joined by 'and': the host must not mint fail/warn other than core policyOutcome, AND must not mint a D9 class, exit or HostTermination from the pack threshold or policyOutcome. The first limb is NT-7's. A harness that retains nothing for it cannot witness half its own claim, and the register's waiver — 'pass all; no waiver by host-minted D9' — leaves no room for a class to go unexercised.
blockers.whatWouldRepairIt: Retain NT-7's evidence explicitly: digest-pinned host paths that derive fail or warn other than from the core policyOutcome in CoreCompletion, paired with pinned refusal bytes showing NT-7 passVerbatim. Then say which member carries it — either as a fourth retained item bound to the claim's first limb, or as a named limb of EV-2 with its own retained bytes — and correct the suppliedBy strings so each member names the class that supplies it. The repair overlaps B2's and both should land together.

blockers.title: The two-class corpus has no specification: neither NT-7's nor NT-8's name, input or pass is quoted, there is no corpus-class object, and every suppliedBy names a single unnamed class
blockers.location: the absence of any corpus-class object; namedExecutesLimbs; retainedEvidence[*].suppliedBy
blockers.finding: The artifact's purpose promises exact-byte intent for 'every live G28 retained-evidence member and the live NT-7/NT-8 host-must-not-mint corpus'. It delivers the members and not the corpus. I enumerated the top-level keys: there is no namedCorpusClasses, no liveNtVerbatim, and no class-level exactByteIntent or passProperty. I then searched for the classes' live text and found none of it — neither the name 'host-must-not-mint-verdict' nor 'host-must-not-mint-d9-or-termination-from-policy' occurs, and neither class's input or pass occurs. All the corpus gets is namedExecutesLimbs ['NT-7', 'NT-8'], two bare ids. The suppliedBy strings compound it: all three read 'host-must-not-mint corpus class' — singular, unnamed — for a corpus the live cell says has two classes, so no member is mapped to the class that supplies it. That singular phrasing is what makes B1 invisible on the page: with no per-class mapping there is nothing to reveal that all three members map to one of the two classes. This is the same defect class as the blocker I raised against the G25 sibling at v1, which that lineage repaired at v2 by adding a corpus-class object carrying the class's name, input and pass verbatim from this same contract, plus class-level intent and pass. The repair idiom already exists in the corpus, one gate over, on the same source artifact.
blockers.failureScenario: A fixture author has the three member intents and two bare NT ids. To learn what NT-7 and NT-8 actually require they must leave this specification, find preview-analyze-contract.v2 unaided — the artifact does pin v2, which is the one thing that saves this from being unrecoverable — and reconcile two classes against three members with no mapping. That reconciliation is what a specification exists to have done already, and doing it is how B1 is found.
blockers.whatWouldRepairIt: Add a namedCorpusClasses array with an object per class carrying nameVerbatim, inputVerbatim and passVerbatim quoted from preview-analyze-contract.v2 negativeTests, the source path, a class-level exactByteIntent and passProperty, and the members each class supplies — the shape the G25 v2 sibling now uses. Then make every suppliedBy name its class.

shouldFix.title: EV-1's pass property is quantified over the D9 v1.14 closed set, and the artifact never pins or even names the artifact that defines it
shouldFix.finding: EV-1's exactByteIntent requires host-emitted D9 class tokens to be 'members of the already-existing D9 v1.14 closed set', and its passProperty scores exactly that membership. The artifact depends on that set eight times by the string 'v1.14' and never says where it lives: the string 'd9-exit-contract' occurs zero times, and basedOn carries only preview-analyze-contract.v2, D-154, D-078 and D-056. The set is not hypothetical — docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json is on disk at 8dd3303855f49bfdbb2751ee65f54a906405f0654159ebe815472f73cdf7da31 — and neither is the ambiguity idle, since fourteen d9-exit-contract versions sit beside it in the same directory. The refusal to enumerate or invent the tokens is exactly right and I am not asking for it to be reversed; a membership test needs a pinned set to test against, not the tokens copied out. Every sibling specification pins what it consumes, and this is the one consumed source this artifact leaves unnamed.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Twelve attacks run, five landed. Custody holds: subject ad5a17b3 at 0444, 5369 bytes, unmoved and unedited; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 equal to the subject's own pin; required-now 26 of 26. Three of three cited digests reproduce. What it carries is accurate — five register cells character-exact, three live members matching the semicolon split, each with an exactByteIntent, a passProperty and a suppliedBy — and the gate's central prohibition is honoured: no D9 class, exit or HostTermination appears, and EV-1 expressly declines to enumerate the v1.14 tokens, which is the right refusal. The first blocker is a coverage hole specific to this gate. The live harness cell names two classes, and against preview-analyze-contract.v2 they are different obligations: NT-7 refuses a host path that derives fail or warn other than from the core policyOutcome in CoreCompletion; NT-8 refuses minting a D9 class, exit or HostTermination from the pack threshold or policyOutcome. I mapped every member and every retained byte onto them, and all three sit inside NT-8. Nothing retains a fail-or-warn derivation path: the string 'fail/warn' occurs twice in the artifact, both in prose and neither in any exactByteIntent, and 'CoreCompletion' occurs zero times. NT-7's property survives only as the second sentence of EV-2's passProperty — a property scored with no bytes retained for it, the inverse of the defect I raised against the G25 sibling and worse in effect, because a reader scanning pass properties sees the obligation covered. A fixture author would build three NT-8 fixtures, run green, and never exercise half this gate's claim, which is two limbs joined by 'and' with the first limb entirely NT-7's. The second blocker is why the first is invisible. The two-class corpus has no specification at all: no corpus-class object, and neither class's name, input nor pass occurs anywhere — I searched all six strings and found none. All the corpus gets is two bare ids, and every suppliedBy reads 'host-must-not-mint corpus class', singular and unnamed, so no member is mapped to the class that supplies it and nothing on the page reveals that three members serve one class. The repair idiom already exists one gate over: the G25 sibling was rejected at v1 for this defect and repaired it at v2 with a corpus-class object quoting name, input and pass verbatim from this same contract. Both blockers should land together. The SHOULD-FIX is a missing pin rather than a missing refusal: EV-1's pass property is quantified over the D9 v1.14 closed set, the artifact depends on that set eight times, and the string 'd9-exit-contract' occurs zero times — while fourteen versions of that contract sit in the same directory and v1.14 is on disk at 8dd33038. Pin it in basedOn and keep the non-enumeration clause exactly as written. Two advisories: the assurance-stage and status cells its own G25 sibling carries are dropped, and no self-test convention is present — no failsIf, no whatThisCloses, no OBL- identifier for a recorder to attach to; and namedExecutesLimbs carries bare NT ids against the live DR-131/DR-133 NT-7 collision, recoverable only because the quoted harness cell carries the row scope.
